data.one_liner: UI toolkit and theming system designed for the Omarchy Arch Linux desktop environment.
data.what_it_does: Provides a comprehensive set of terminal-styled widgets and overlays matching the Omarchy aesthetic. Automatically reads system color palettes and Alacritty configs from local files to synchronize theme changes in real time. Also supports running on other platforms by falling back to a default Tokyonight theme.
use_when: Building Flutter desktop applications specifically targeting the Omarchy Arch Linux setup
Creating applications with a minimalist, terminal-inspired keyboard-friendly desktop aesthetic
Needing real-time integration with local Linux system theme files without app restarts
avoid_when: Building mainstream consumer mobile apps that require standard Material or Cupertino design
Needing an enterprise-tested, highly stable production UI framework (package is in early development with unstable APIs)
strengths: Rich collection of specialized desktop widgets (split panels, command panels, context menus, status bars)
Automatic hot-reloading of themes from system TOML files and signals
Cross-platform fallback to Tokyonight theme for testing outside Linux
weaknesses: Under active early development with self-admitted unstable APIs
Requires manual adjustments to Linux GTK runner code to eliminate title bars or black startup windows
data.setup_notes: Requires `await Omarchy.initialize()` in main. Linux deployment may require manual modifications in linux/runner/my_application.cc to hide titlebars and prevent black startup windows.
